To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AKR-MCAs and AKR-2Bs have different cytosolic protein phosphorylation patterns and that the dimethylformamide-induced restoration of normal phenotype is associated with a change in cytosolic phosphorylation patterns.

the AKR-MCAs have a different pattern of phosphorylated proteins in their cytosol than do the untransformed AKRs, and that treatment with dimethyl formide restores some but not all of the normal phosphorylation pattern.

the malignant AKR-MCA phenotype can be restored to a phenotype similar, but not identical, to the normal untransformed AKRI-2B phenotype by treatment of the malignant cells with dimethyl-formamide, and that the malignant AKRI-MCA phenotype can also be restored to a normal phenotype by treatment of AKR-MC A cells with transforming growth factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of protein phosphorylation in normal and malignant mouse cells and with the effects of various agents, including transforming growth factor and dimethylformamide, on these processes.

the identification and characterization of protein kinase-phosphoproteins which are associated with malignant transformation of AKR mouse embryo cells and the restoration of normal cell phenotype by the chemical carcinogen, methylcholanthene, and by the growth factor, transforming growth factor.
the study of the biochemical events involved in the process of malignant transformation of cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AKR-MCAs are transformed and that the dimethylformamide-treated AKR-MCAn cells are partially reverted to the untransformed AKRs.
the protein kinase-phosphotase system in the cytosol of AKR-MCAs is qualitatively different from that of AKR- 2Bs.
there were differences in the phosphorylation patterns of cytosol protein substrates between normal and transformed AKR cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the AKR-MC-transformed phenotype is associated with the loss or alteration of some normal cell protein kinase-phosphoprotein activities and the acquisition of other kinase-phosphoproteins which are not normally observed in untransformed AKr-2B cells.

the transformation of AKR cells with methylcholanthrenes is a complex process involving multiple changes in protein kinases and/or phosphatases, and that these changes are reversible by the treatment of the transformed cells with dimethyl-formamide.
we have identified several proteins whose phosphorylation is altered during the transformation of normal mouse embryo fibroblast cells by chemical carcinogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AKR-Mca cells are not a good model for cancer.
the phosphorylation of cytoplasmic proteins is altered during transformation, and these changes are reversible in the presence of dimethylformamide.

there is a change in the protein kinase-phosphorylase activity in the AKR MCA cells compared to the AKR 2B cells and that the treatment with DMF is able to restore some of the normal protein kinase-phosphotase activity.
